text:
anna: FYI hit a weird NDCG/MRR wobble after PTQ on the new reranker when candidate pool size changes. small repro attached in thread below.
marc: ugh. is this on the holdout or a prod slice?
sara: holdout. seed-fixed eval harness.
anna: holdout. baseline fp16 vs int8. for pool sizes 10/50/200 we see ndcg10 drop ~3.5% at 50 but returns at 200. mrr also flips for short queries.
josh: can you paste the config and metric numbers?
anna: sure —
```
model: rerank-v3
quant: dynamic-ptq-int8
seed: 42
candidate_pool_sizes: [10,50,200]
metric: ndcg@10, mrr
preproc: truncate_docs=1024, query_trunc=64, doc_concat=false
```
anna: results: fp16 ndcg@10: [0.412, 0.421, 0.409] int8: [0.407, 0.406, 0.410]
marc: hmm int8 loses at 10 and 50 then recovers at 200. sounds like candidate ordering sensitivity. maybe quantized logits tie-breaking differs.
sara: could be scale/embedding rescale interaction if we normalize candidate texts differently. did you try candidate shuffling determinism?
anna: harness is deterministic. tried different seeds, same pattern. also observed short-query subset shows bigger MRR dip.
josh: can you run a tiny probe: pass the same pool but normalize doc casing and whitespace, compare ndcg delta. might isolate formatting frag.
anna: running now, will post link to temp artifact.
eval-bot: CI smoke: rerank-v3/int8/candidates-50 — ndcg10 delta -0.014 vs fp16 — flaky
ops-bot: reminder: if you post artifacts, use s3://redwood-evals/private/ for holdout data
anna: artifact link s3://redwood-evals/private/4299001234/probe-normalize.tar.gz
sara: quick thought — are we using different quantization scales per head vs per-tensor? headwise int8 can amplify small ordering shifts.
marc: good point. what quant backend? x86 PTQ or cuda kernel fbgemm?
anna: PTQ run used per-channel affine scales on weights, activation calibrated per-layer. backend = fbgemm on cpu bench, cuda uses symmetric per-tensor for runtime.
josh: that mismatch could explain environment-dependent deltas. try aligning runtime quant backend to calibration config and rerun.
anna: queued a run: same quant params but force cuda per-tensor calibration to match runtime. posted when done.
sara: also thinking about sample weighting — our holdout has long-tail docs. try slicing by candidate effective length to see if the "recovery at 200" is because longer docs get in pool and the model favors them when more candidates present.
anna: good idea. I'll slice by avg_doc_tokens and short-query boolean.
josh: if repro holds, let's add a tiny gating rule to bringup checklist: 1) candidate-pool sweep (10/50/200) 2) slice-by-querylen 3) backend parity check 4) seed reproducibility 5) quick calibration delta <0.5% ndcg
marc: agreed. also add a small deterministic rerank smoke script for CI that runs 100 samples and compares top1 agreement between fp16/int8.
anna: adding script now. snippet:
```
python smoke_rerank.py --model rerank-v3 --quant int8 --samples 100 --pool_sizes 10,50,200 --out /tmp/smoke.json
```
anna: running both alignment and slicing runs, will report numbers shortly.
marc: thanks. if it's a quant backend mismatch we can patch the runtime or add calibration hints to the PTQ pipeline; if it's formatting, fix preproc canonicalization.
sara: also logging for papertrail: link to thread + artifacts is in ticket ML-4312
josh: 👍 once we have repro we should decide canary thresholds for Dedicated vs Hosted rollout.
anna: update 4299001262: after forcing backend parity and normalizing whitespace/case, int8 ndcg@10 = [0.410, 0.419, 0.411] — gap narrowed to ~0.002 for pool 50. looks like a combo of quant backend mismatch + minor formatting frag.
marc: great find. next: add a unit in quant pipeline to assert calibration/runtime parity and add canonicalizer to preproc.
sara: i'll capture the slicing breakdown and add to the eval dashboard.
anna: thanks all. filing PR for pipeline checks and adding smoke_rerank to premerge CI. :thumbsup:
